diagnostic_evidence.quote: While our architecture inherently ensures symplecticity, exact Hamiltonian conservation is not enforced, as the proposed architecture only guarantees an approximate Hamiltonian is enforced.
we introduce an additional Hamiltonian conservation constraint:

issues.failure_explanation: The prose asserts that the symplectic architecture ensures energy conservation. A symplectic map need not preserve any given Hamiltonian; the paper itself states in Section 4.3 that exact Hamiltonian conservation is not enforced and adds a penalty loss to promote it only approximately. Nothing in the source establishes energy conservation as a structural guarantee.

failure_location.quote: In summary, our architecture maintains the symplectic structure of the original system, ensuring energy conservation and numerical stability through nonlinear transformations.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the claim to 'exact symplecticity, with approximate Hamiltonian preservation promoted by the loss term'.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantee of energy conservation is unsupported; only approximate, loss-driven Hamiltonian preservation is demonstrated numerically.
issues.title: Introduction claims symplecticity ensures energy conservation, contradicted by the paper's own admission
issues.why_classification: A local rewording aligns the claim with what the paper actually establishes; no result or method is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: For H(V,eta)(x,y)=(y+eta, x+grad V(y)) the Jacobian is D=[[0,I],[I,H_V]] and D^T J_{2n} D = -J_{2n}, so the map reverses the symplectic form (it is anti-symplectic). The standard Hénon map (as used in the cited Turaev/Burby results and as the paper itself uses in the nonlinear embedding via -P x) has -x in the second component. The inverse formula in prop:added-1 is consistent with the anti-symplectic version, so correcting the sign also forces a change of the inverse; the cited universal-approximation result does not directly apply to the map as written.

failure_location.quote: The fundamental building block is the H\'enon mapping, which enables intricate nonlinear transformations while preserving symplectic structure:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace x by -x in the definition and correspondingly change the inverse to (-v + grad V(u-eta), u-eta), or state that H is anti-symplectic and only H^2 and H^4 are symplectic.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the building block preserves symplectic structure is false as written; the Hénon layer [H]^4 remains symplectic (an even power of an anti-symplectic map), so layer-level and network-level symplecticity survive.
issues.title: Hénon mapping as defined is anti-symplectic, not symplectic
issues.why_classification: Local sign correction with a matching adjustment of the inverse; all downstream symplecticity guarantees are preserved because the layer is a fourth power.

issues.failure_explanation: For k<n the condition iota^+ iota = I_{2k} has infinitely many solutions (any left inverse of the rank-2k matrix iota), so it does not uniquely define iota^+; the unique symplectic inverse is J_{2k}^T iota^T J_{2n} from eq:symplectic-inverse. Moreover iota^+ is 2k x 2n, so (iota^+)^T J_{2n} is a product of a 2n x 2k and a 2n x 2n matrix and is undefined; the valid identity is iota^+ J_{2n} (iota^+)^T = J_{2k}.

failure_location.quote: The symplectic pseudo-inverse $\iota^+$ is uniquely defined by the condition $\iota^+ \iota = I_{2k}$ and satisfies $(\iota^+)^T J_{2n} \iota^+ = J_{2k}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define iota^+ := J_{2k}^T iota^T J_{2n} and replace the identity by iota^+ J_{2n} (iota^+)^T = J_{2k}.
issues.overall_effect: The characterization of the inverse composite embedding (def:inverse-composite) rests on an incorrect description, though the intended object J_{2k}^T iota^T J_{2n} (equal to the truncation tau) is correct.
issues.title: Symplectic pseudo-inverse mischaracterized: not unique from left-inverse condition and stated identity is dimensionally ill-formed
issues.why_classification: Purely local correction of a definition; the actual object used (tau) is correct and nothing downstream changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The universal approximation capability of H\'enonNets implies that any symplectic diffeomorphism, including the nonlinear embedding defined above, can be approximated arbitrarily closely by composing a fixed linear embedding with H\'enonNet transformations.
This composite structure possesses universal approximation capability for symplectic embeddings, as formalized in the following theorem:
H\'enonNet has been proven to possess a universal approximation theorem for nonlinear symplectic mappings~\cite{turaev2002polynomial}

issues.failure_explanation: No proof is given. The only support is the cited universal approximation of symplectic diffeomorphisms of R^{2n} by HénonNets. Applying it to sigma = H∘G∘iota requires that the target embedding Phi factor as Psi∘iota on Omega for some global symplectomorphism Psi of R^{2n}; this nontrivial extension step (a symplectic-neighborhood plus isotopy-extension argument, valid e.g. for ball-shaped Omega) is neither stated nor proved, and the embedding g of eq:nonlinear-sym-lift is not a 'symplectic diffeomorphism' as the prose says. Worse, the statement is false for arbitrary compact Omega: with k=n=1 (allowed, SpSt(2n,2n)=Sp(2n)), take Omega the annulus 1<=|z|<=2 and Phi a radial area-preserving map onto a<=|z|<=sqrt(a^2+3) with a≠1. Any sigma = HénonNet∘G is a global area-preserving diffeomorphism of R^2, so sigma(|z|=1) is a Jordan curve enclosing area pi, whereas a curve uniformly epsilon-close to Phi(|z|=1) (a circle of radius a) encloses area near pi a^2 or near 0; hence sup|Phi-sigma| cannot be made small. Thus 'arbitrary symplectic embedding on a compact domain' cannot be approximated.

failure_location.quote: Let $\Phi:\mathbb{R}^{2k}\to \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ be an arbitrary symplectic embedding defined on a compact domain $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^{2k}$. For any $\varepsilon>0$, there exist parameters of \(\iota, \mathcal{G},\) and \(\text{H}\)  such that the composite map \(\sigma\) defined in \eqref{eq:composite} satisfies

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the theorem to embeddings Phi that extend to (or are restrictions of) a global symplectomorphism of R^{2n} composed with iota—e.g. Omega a closed ball, using an Alexander-trick isotopy plus symplectic isotopy extension—and then invoke the HénonNet universal approximation on compacts, supplying this argument explicitly.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised 'universal approximation guarantee' for the composite embedding architecture (and the justification for fixing iota rather than learning P) is unsupported; a comparable result holds only under additional hypotheses on Omega/Phi (e.g. Phi extends to a global symplectomorphism, or Omega is a ball) and requires a genuine proof.
issues.title: Universal approximation theorem for symplectic embeddings is unproven and false as stated for general compact domains
issues.why_classification: A recognizably comparable theorem survives for restricted domains, but the repair needs a contained nontrivial extension argument and a restriction of the stated scope; it does not overturn the methodology, which is validated numerically.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For a formally complete parametrization, $4n$ G-reflector layers are needed.

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own statement, completeness of the G-reflector parameterization of Sp(2n) requires 4n layers; with Delta x = 0.005 (N = 200, n = 200) that is 800 layers, whereas the experiments use 100 (or 10) layers, which do not parameterize all of Sp(2n) and hence not all of SpSt(2k,2n). For the HénonNet-based embedding only approximate (density-type) representability is claimed, not an exact 'complete parameterization', and that claim is itself unproven (ISSUE-004).

failure_location.quote: It is worth emphasizing again that the cotangent lift is an incomplete parameterization of $\mathrm{SpSt}(2k,2n)$, whereas the others offer complete parameterizations of the corresponding linear or non-linear symplectic embedding manifolds.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword to say the G-reflector construction can be made complete with 4n layers but a truncated stack is used, and that HénonNets are (conjecturally/under hypotheses) dense rather than complete.
issues.overall_effect: The stated interpretation of the reconstruction-MSE comparison (complete vs. incomplete parameterization) is not supported for the architectures actually tested.
issues.title: Overclaim that the tested G-reflector and HénonNet embeddings are complete parameterizations
issues.why_classification: A local wording change; numerical comparisons themselves are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $a_0\in [7,9]$, $x_0\in[-0.2,0.2]$, and $\omega$ represents the wave speed.
integrating numerically over $[0,12]$ using the St{\"o}rmer-Verlet scheme

issues.failure_explanation: u(x,t)=u^0(x-omega t) is the free-space d'Alembert solution, but the problem is posed on [0,1] with homogeneous Dirichlet conditions. The initial bump has support radius 2/a_0 around 1/2+x_0 and travels rightward, reaching x=1 in finite time (e.g. for x_0=0, u(1,t)=u^0(1-omega t)=h(a_0|1/2-omega t|)=1 at omega t=1/2), after which the formula violates u(1,t)=0 and the true solution reflects. The cross-reference also points to the spline definition rather than the PDE.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the formula as valid only until the wave reaches the boundary (or on the whole line), and fix the equation reference.
issues.overall_effect: The stated 'exact solution' is incorrect on the simulated time interval; the numerical reference data (Störmer–Verlet on the discretized Dirichlet problem) is unaffected, so only the analytic claim is wrong.
issues.title: Claimed exact traveling-wave solution violates the Dirichlet boundary conditions of the posed problem
issues.why_classification: Local correction of an unused side statement; no result or experiment depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \frac{d}{d t} \mathbf{z}=\bbJ_{2 N} \nabla_{\bf z} H({\bf z})=\bbJ_{2 N} L\mathbf{z} + \bbJ_{2 N}\mathbf{g}(\bf z),

issues.failure_explanation: For the canonical system eq:schro-can with J=[[0,I],[-I,0]] one needs delta H/delta p = p_xx + eps(q^2+p^2)p, i.e. H_cont = -1/2∫(q_x^2+p_x^2) + eps/4∫(q^2+p^2)^2. The printed H_cont has the gradient and quartic terms with the same sign (and wrong factors); it is not a conserved quantity of the stated focusing NLS (∫|u|^4 alone is not conserved). The printed discrete H squares the products (q_{i-1}q_i - q_i^2)^2 (a quartic, not a discretization of q_x^2) and uses a quadratic eps/4(p_i^2+q_i^2) instead of eps/4(p_i^2+q_i^2)^2; its gradient is not L z + eps g(z) as claimed (g also omits eps). Two independent corrections are needed, so this is not a single forced typo.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace H_cont by -1/2∫(q_x^2+p_x^2)+eps/4∫(q^2+p^2)^2 (or flip the sign convention consistently), remove the squares on the difference terms and square the nonlinear term in eq:schro-ham-discre, and include eps in g.
issues.overall_effect: The Hamiltonian entering the conservation loss eq:loss-ham and the diagnostics of Figure schro-ham is misstated for Example ex:schro; if used as printed it would penalize/monitor a non-conserved functional. The dynamics themselves are correctly specified.
issues.title: Stated continuous and discrete Hamiltonians for the NLS example are inconsistent with the stated dynamics
issues.why_classification: Local corrections to displayed formulas restore consistency; the method and reported experiments are not structurally affected.
